mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in INDPRO (index below 100 for two consecutive months) signals a manufacturing slowdown, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals a broad-based deterioration in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise together for three consecutive months, it indicates a combination of tighter policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which initially supports consumer spending but eventually leads to higher wage costs and inflation, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in a late-cycle expansion regime.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% growth for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered late-cycle episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 1% for five consecutive months signals a surge in household savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumption and weaker corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days unless offset by external demand drivers.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 1% growth for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
